title: A Satellite Captures the Sun Every 12 Seconds
description: Since 2010, NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory has been observing the Sun continuously across multiple wavelengths. This constant watch reveals towering coronal loops, powerful flares, and complex magnetic activity.

shots.narration: Since 2010, the Solar Dynamics Observatory has imaged the Sun every twelve seconds across several different wavelengths.
Transmitting 1.5 terabytes of data daily, the observatory monitors a star measuring 1.39 million kilometres across.
Across that immense solar disk, 109 Earths could fit side by side.
While the visible surface is 5,500 °C, the thin outer corona reaches over a million degrees.
In these active regions, glowing plasma traces magnetic field lines high above the surface.
A single towering magnetic loop in the solar atmosphere can be larger than many Earths.
When active regions erupt, a large flare releases energy equal to millions of hydrogen bombs.
Light from the eruption reaches Earth in 8 minutes 20 seconds; particle clouds take one to three days.
Every eleven years, this continuous magnetic activity causes the Sun's magnetic poles to swap places.
